name: Emigre
summary: A magazine of design and typography that Rudy VanderLans edited and designed, with type by Zuzana Licko on a Macintosh. At first it came out quarterly. By 1986 the foundry Emigre Fonts sold her digital typefaces. The magazine ended in 2005 with issue 69.

statement.text: Licko replied to critics that people read best what they read most.
statement.title: Summary of a reply by Licko

moves.text: VanderLans and two Dutch friends, whom he met in San Francisco, founded the magazine.
By 1986 Emigre sold licences of its digital fonts under the name Emigre Fonts.
Massimo Vignelli called the work of Emigre garbage in an interview in Print, which brought the studio more attention.
The magazine ended with its last issue, The End.

sources.title: Rudy VanderLans and Zuzana Licko, Emigre: Graphic Design into the Digital Realm (Van Nostrand Reinhold, 1993)
